judgments.reasoning_cat2: It empowers the Board to override restrictions that Sections 14.3 and 13.1 place in the hands of all Members unanimously — a direct allocation-of-power conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Methods of delivery are enumerated and the deemed-receipt rule is explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Notices to the Company go to the Section 2.5 address, which the Board may change unilaterally, and no notice address is given for the Company's officers; a minor loose end only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The double-negative construction ("shall not prevent a subsequent act ... from having the effect of an original violation") is convoluted and the final phrase is capitalised oddly, but the anti-waiver sense is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 17.3's cumulative-remedies clause; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard cumulative-remedies boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforces Section 17.2; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short binding-effect clause with an internal limitation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "to the extent permitted by this Agreement" qualifier defers correctly to Articles XIV and XVI on assigns.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional gender/number and cross-reference construction rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its promise that references correspond to provisions of this Agreement is undercut by the phantom references to Sections 6.9 and 16.9-16.11, though that failing belongs to those sections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard severability wording; the stray period mid-sentence is immaterial.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision conditions the Agreement's validity on any particular clause surviving.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary counterparts clause, determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Sections 2.1(ii) and 13.1, which contemplate execution of counterparts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Pertaining to the subject matter hereof" leaves the superseded field undefined, which is the usual battleground for integration clauses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.7's service and exclusivity undertakings blur the line between this operating agreement and any employment or compensation arrangement that this clause would supersede.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Single choice-of-law sentence expressly excluding conflicts principles.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Maine Act references throughout; the Massachusetts location of the business does not create an internal conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires both an affirmative vote of all Members and a writing executed by all; clear if slightly redundant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(iii) lets the Secretary revise Schedule A — which fixes Percentage Interests and Member Votes — and declares such revisions not amendments, an evident route around this unanimity requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short no-third-party-beneficiary clause; the exception for "Members and Managers" is defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Covered Persons under Sections 12.2-12.5 include employees and agents who are neither Members nor Managers, yet this clause denies them rights — a mild internal tension.
